answer_1.quote: We showcase its effectiveness in both Multi-document Summarization (MDS) and Long-form Question-answering (LFQA)...
answer_1.outputs: summaries and long-form answers accompanied by sentence‑level citations

answer_2.quote: We employ ROUGE L and BERTSCORE metrics... For assessing citation conciseness, we report the average length (number of tokens) of the cited content per output sentence. To evaluate citation quality, we employ AUTOAIS, an NLI‑based metric for attribution evaluation.

answer_4.quote: Human Evaluation. The evaluation of generated attributed texts consists of two steps. First, annotators are asked to evaluate text coherence on a 5‑point Likert scale, and in the LFQA setting also its helpfulness. Next, annotators proceed to evaluate the quality of citations... We used the Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) crowdsourcing platform.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate text coherence, helpfulness (for LFQA), and citation support (full/partial/no support) using provided criteria.
